guideTitle: 6 Best Stainless Steel Salad Spinners in 2026
metaDescription: Six stainless steel salad spinners compared on 304 versus 18/8 steel, lock lids, crank versus pump drives and storage lids, from 4.8 to 6.22 quarts.
introParagraphs: Stainless steel salad spinners are popular because the bowl does not stain, hold odors or scratch the way plastic can. The catch is that nearly every one still has a plastic lid, gears or spin mechanism, so the steel only covers part of the story. What separates the good ones is how the lid locks, how you spin the basket and whether the listing says anything about cleaning.

The six spinners below range from 4.8 to 6.22 quarts. Most are 5.3 quart models that name 304 stainless steel, while the SveBake 4.8 quart uses 18/8 steel and the OXO has the pump drive. We evaluated specs and listing details and note where a feature is not stated, so you can check the product page for anything that matters to you.

Think about drive style first, then lid design, then size, because those three decisions affect daily use far more than the badge on the box. Capacity and drive style are the two numbers worth writing down before you compare, since four of these six share the same 5.3 quart bowl and differ mainly in lid design, drive and extras such as the storage lid on the Lytycjd or the lock-on lid on the BOMANSI. Where two picks look alike on paper, the tie-breaker is usually how you plan to store the finished greens.

products.name: OXO Good Grips Stainless Steel Salad Spinner, 6.22 Qt
products.description:
The OXO stainless spinner pairs a steel bowl with a soft-touch one-handed pump, and the listing also names a wide non-slip base and a built-in brake button that stops the basket instantly. The bowl is described as suitable for spinning, serving and storage, which gives it more uses than a spin-only design. With no cord or plug, it runs entirely by hand.

The 6.22 quarts is the largest capacity in this group, so it handles a full head of lettuce or a family salad. The tradeoff is the size and the steel weight, which means it takes cabinet room. The listing does not name the steel grade, so check the product page if grade matters to you.

The pump is the main difference from the crank spinners here. Compared with the Lytycjd crank model at 5.3 quarts, the OXO leaves one hand free and gives roughly a quart more room. Against the SveBake 5.3 quart with its one-touch stop, the OXO adds a pump drive and a larger bowl. If ease of use is your top priority, this is the one to pick.
products.bestFor: Anyone who wants a steel bowl with easy one-handed pump operation.
pros: One-handed pump leaves a hand free
Instant brake button stops the basket
Wide non-slip base keeps it steady
cons: Steel grade not named in the listing

products.name: BOMANSI BOMS 5.3 Qt Stainless Steel Salad Spinner
products.description:
BOMANSI uses 304 stainless steel for both the outer bowl and the inner basket, which is more steel than most spinners offer. The lid is a lock-on design that the listing says keeps things spill-free while spinning. A silicone base grips the countertop and is meant to prevent wobbling at high speed.

The lock-lid is the standout, since a loose lid is a common complaint with spinning baskets. The listing excerpt does not state how the basket is turned, so check the product page for crank, knob or pump details. Like any steel bowl, it is opaque and heavier than plastic.

At 5.3 quarts it is about a quart smaller than the OXO but matches the SveBake and Lunememo in size. Compared with the SveBake, the BOMANSI adds steel on the basket as well as the bowl and a lock-on lid. Against the Lytycjd, which also names 304 steel for bowl and basket, BOMANSI emphasizes lid security rather than a storage lid. It suits buyers who want steel throughout and a lid that stays put.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want 304 steel on bowl and basket plus a lid that locks.
cons: Drive style not stated in the excerpt

products.name: Lytycjd 5.3 Qt Stainless Steel Salad Spinner
products.description:
Lytycjd names a complete 304 stainless steel system, with a steel outer bowl, a perforated steel basket and a locking lid. It uses an easy-grip hand crank for spinning, and the listing says the steel bowl and basket are dishwasher safe. A silicone lid is included so you can cover the bowl and put it in the fridge after spinning.

The storage lid is the practical difference, since you can wash, spin and store greens in the same bowl. The crank gives you control over speed, but it needs a turning motion and usually a second hand to steady the bowl. If you have limited grip, a pump is easier.

Compared with the OXO at 6.22 quarts, the Lytycjd holds about a quart less and replaces the pump with a crank. Against the SveBake 4.8 quart, which also has a crank, the Lytycjd has a larger bowl and a storage lid. Compared with BOMANSI at the same 5.3 quarts, it is the one with the dishwasher-safe steel and the fridge lid. It is a good choice for people who store greens after washing.
products.bestFor: Cooks who want to wash, spin and store greens in one dishwasher-safe steel bowl.

products.name: SveBake Stainless Steel Salad Spinner, 5.3 Qt
products.description:
The SveBake 5.3 quart spinner has a stainless steel bowl with a BPA-free plastic lid and a one-touch stop that the listing says halts the spinning quickly. It is described as sturdy and suitable for long-term use, and it includes an easy drain feature and a non-slip base. The size is generous enough for a large bowl of salad greens.

The steel does not say 304 in the listing excerpt, so grade is unclear, and the plastic lid is the part most likely to wear first. The drive style is also not described in the excerpt, so check the product page. A one-touch stop is useful if you often wait for the basket to slow.

Compared with the OXO at 6.22 quarts, it is smaller and its drive is less clear. Against the BOMANSI at the same capacity, it lacks the explicitly named 304 steel basket but adds the one-touch stop. Compared with the SveBake 4.8 quart crank model, the 5.3 quart version offers more room and a stop button, which makes it the more convenient of the two SveBake options.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a steel bowl and a quick stop at a mid-size capacity.
cons: Steel grade not named in the excerpt
Plastic lid is the wear point

products.name: Lunememo Stainless Steel Salad Spinner, 5.3 Qt
products.description:
Lunememo lists a 5.3 quart bowl made of 304 stainless steel with a sleek look and a non-slip base that keeps the unit planted on the counter. You rotate a handle to spin the basket, and the listing mentions quick dry and stop features. It is suitable for greens, beans, sprouts and microgreens.

The handle is simple, but a rotating handle needs a grip-and-turn motion rather than a push. The listing notes it is BPA free, but the excerpt does not say which parts are plastic, so check the lid and basket on the product page. Steel is opaque and a bit heavy.

Compared with the OXO at 6.22 quarts, it is smaller and uses a handle rather than a pump. Against the Lytycjd, which names both a steel bowl and basket plus a storage lid, the Lunememo is simpler and does not mention a storage lid. Compared with the BOMANSI, it has the same 5.3 quarts but does not list a lock-on lid, so it fits buyers who want straightforward steel without extras.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a plain 304 steel spinner without extra accessories.
cons: Basket and lid materials not clear

products.name: SveBake Stainless Steel Salad Spinner, 4.8 Qt
products.description:
This SveBake model is a 4.8 quart spinner made from 18/8 stainless steel and BPA-free ABS. The listing highlights a crank design with precise control, which the maker says makes it suitable for delicate berries. It also lists easy draining and a non-slip base.

The smaller size makes it easier to store than the 5.3 and 6.22 quart models, and the crank gives you control over spin speed. That control is useful for tender greens and berries that bruise easily. The tradeoff is that a crank usually needs two hands and some wrist motion.

Compared with the SveBake 5.3 quart model, it is about half a quart smaller and uses a crank rather than a one-touch stop. Against the Lytycjd, which also uses a crank, it is smaller and does not list a storage lid. Compared with the OXO at 6.22 quarts, it holds about 1.4 quarts less and lacks a pump, so it is the choice for small households that value speed control and compact storage.
products.bestFor: Small households that want crank speed control for delicate produce.
pros: Gentle on berries and tender greens

buyingCriteria.criterion: Steel grade and what it covers
buyingCriteria.explanation: Listings often say stainless steel without saying how much of the unit is steel. BOMANSI and Lytycjd name 304 steel for both the bowl and the basket, Lunememo names 304 for the bowl, and the SveBake 4.8 quart names 18/8. Many models pair steel with a plastic lid, as the SveBake 5.3 quart does with its BPA-free plastic lid. Look for a listing that names both the grade and which parts are steel.

The drive decides how much effort the spinner takes. The OXO at 6.22 quarts uses a one-handed pump, the Lytycjd and SveBake 4.8 quart use cranks, and the Lunememo uses a rotating handle. A pump leaves one hand free to steady the bowl, which is easier for limited grip. Cranks give more control but usually need both hands.

A lid that pops off at high speed ruins a spin. BOMANSI has a lock-on lid that the listing says keeps things spill-free, and Lytycjd has a locking lid. Check that any model you choose has a lock or a secure fit. For smaller models like the SveBake 4.8 quart, test the lid fit as soon as it arrives.

Steel spinners are heavy, so pick a size you will actually use. The SveBake 4.8 quart suits one or two people, the 5.3 quart BOMANSI, Lytycjd, Lunememo and SveBake suit families, and the OXO at 6.22 quarts suits bigger batches. Remember the basket is smaller than the bowl. If you are unsure, 5.3 quarts is a safe middle.

Steel bowls are tough, but lids and drive parts may not like the dishwasher. The Lytycjd lists a dishwasher-safe steel bowl and basket and includes a silicone storage lid for the fridge. The OXO bowl is described as suitable for serving and storage. Check the product page for dishwasher rules on lids and mechanisms.

A brake and a non-slip base both matter for steel, because a heavy basket spins long after you let go. The OXO has an instant brake button, the SveBake 5.3 quart has a one-touch stop, and BOMANSI and Lunememo use non-slip bases. A stable unit stays put on the counter during spinning. Pick at least one of these features.

howWeEvaluated.title: Steel and materials
howWeEvaluated.description: We read each listing for which parts are steel and which are plastic. BOMANSI and Lytycjd name 304 steel for both bowl and basket, Lunememo names 304 for the bowl, and SveBake 4.8 quart names 18/8. The OXO and SveBake 5.3 quart do not name a grade in the excerpt.

howWeEvaluated.title: Drive and control
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared the pump on the OXO, cranks on the Lytycjd and SveBake 4.8 quart, and the handle on the Lunememo. Pumps scored higher for ease, cranks for control. Models that do not state their drive were flagged.

howWeEvaluated.title: Lid and spill control
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at lock-on and locking lids on BOMANSI and Lytycjd and the plastic lid on the SveBake 5.3 quart. A secure lid scored higher. We also noted storage lids, such as the silicone lid on the Lytycjd.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity and fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared 4.8, 5.3 and 6.22 quart sizes. The OXO leads in capacity, four models cluster at 5.3 quarts, and the SveBake 4.8 quart suits small households. Bigger is not always better for storage.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cleaning and stability
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked dishwasher notes, non-slip bases and brakes. The Lytycjd lists dishwasher-safe steel, the OXO has a brake button, and BOMANSI uses a silicone base. Anything unstated was marked as something to check.

faq.a: They are very similar in practice, since both are common food-grade austenitic steels. BOMANSI, Lytycjd and Lunememo name 304, and the SveBake 4.8 quart names 18/8. Focus more on which parts are steel and how the lid fits.

faq.q: Is a stainless steel salad spinner dishwasher safe?
faq.a: The Lytycjd lists a dishwasher-safe steel bowl and basket. For the others, check the product page, especially for lids and drive parts. When in doubt, hand wash the lid and mechanism.

faq.q: Why does my steel spinner still have plastic parts?
faq.a: Most models use steel for the bowl and plastic for the lid and gears, like the SveBake 5.3 quart with its BPA-free plastic lid. That keeps weight down and the mechanism affordable. Check the listing to see what is steel.

faq.q: Which is easiest to use with weak hands?
faq.a: A one-handed pump like the OXO at 6.22 quarts is the easiest in this group. Cranks and handles need more turning. Look for non-slip bases to avoid holding the bowl tightly.

faq.q: Can I put greens in the fridge in the spinner?
faq.a: The Lytycjd includes a silicone storage lid for this, and the OXO bowl is described as suitable for storage. Dry the greens well first. Check the product page for the other models.

faq.q: Do steel spinners dry greens better than plastic?
faq.a: The drying power depends on the basket and spin speed, not the bowl material. Steel mainly adds durability and stain resistance. Pick based on drive and lid rather than material alone. If drying speed matters, pay attention to how smoothly the basket spins and whether the base stays put, because a wobbling unit slows you down more than the bowl material ever will.

faq.q: How do I prevent rust or spots?
faq.a: Dry the bowl and basket after washing, and avoid leaving salty or acidic dressing in the bowl. Quality steel resists rust but can still spot. Wipe it dry before storing.
